answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and zero buffer, an immediate vendor switch is the highest-risk path even though memory_c2 suggests it yielded sharp unit-cost savings; I want c2 verified to know whether the switching savings were real and low-friction, since that determines the fallback if negotiation falls short of the 18% mandate. Meanwhile, memory_c4 and memory_c6 indicate the incumbent has moved on both price and terms when benchmarked, and multi-year structure cut unit cost without narrowing scope — so renegotiating at this expiry is the one action that targets the mandated cut without adding delivery risk in the 14-day window. If verified c2 shows switching truly was quick and clean, a guarded switch with the incumbent retained as secondary (per c3's dual-source logic) becomes the fallback for the next review.
